Purchase Agreement for  Resolution  No  22- 04 -  Purchase Aareement for Meter Read Devices -
Meter Read  Devices  The City currently bills approximately 8, 700 accounts bi- monthly.
  Approximately 800 of those accounts are radio reads, or Automated Meter
  Reading ( AMR). The current meter read devices( Handhelds) and AMR
  accessories  were  purchased  in 2008 from National Meter.  National  Meter

  notified City staff that our handhelds and AMR accessories are no longer
  supported.  Additionally, National Meter discontinued technical support of
  the software used for transferring the meter reads to the billing system.

  Public Works Director Igoe recommended  that the City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 22- 04 approving a purchase from Core and Main, Inc. for the
  budgeted purchase of Meter Read Devices and replacement of the current
  Automated Meter Reading ( AMR) System, not to exceed the amount of
  190, 000 for the AMR Meter Device Update Project; and to authorize the City
  Manager or his Designee to enter into a contract with Core and Main, Inc. for
  the purchase of Meter Read Devices and replacement of the current
  Automated Meter Metering Reading ( AMR) System, for the AMR Meter Device
  Update Project.

  Mandatory Organic Waste  City Manager Russi introduced the Mandatory Organic Waste Disposal
  Disposal  Regulations -  Regulations and recommendation to amend the La Verne Municipal Code by
  Amending  the  La Verne  adding Chapter 13. 30. He stated that Public Works Manager Costello would
  Municipal Code  by Adding  report on the item. Public Works Manager Costello stated that Senate Bill
  Chapter 13. 30  1383 ( SB 1383),  the Short- lived Climate Pollutant Reduction Act of 2016,
  requires jurisdictions  to adopt and enforce an ordinance  or another
  enforceable mechanism requiring organic waste to be diverted from landfills.
  In accordance with SB 1383, all jurisdictions must have a mandatory organic
  waste  disposal reduction ordinance in place. Each year the City is required to
  demonstrate compliance efforts in the Electronic Annual Report( EAR)
  submitted to CalRecycle, the State' s regulatory agency that oversees
  California' s State- managed waste handling and recycling programs.

  In addition, she reported that in November of 2020, the repeal and replace of
  Chapter 13. 28 Collection, Removal and Disposal of Refuse went into effect. In
  Section 13. 28. 010( E) Declaration of Policy, mandatory compliance with SB
  1383 was established. The City Attorney reviewed the municipal code
  requirements of SB 1383 and determined staff should implement relevant
  provisions of SB 1383 Regulations to the City Municipal Code for further
  clarification  and enforcement  purposes.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this item.

  There was  one  public  comment  at  the meeting. (  To hear what was said during
  public comment, please visit the City' s website to view the archived Council
  meeting.)

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Carder, and unanimously carried by roll
  call to introduce, waive further reading and place on first reading Ordinance
  No. 1109, adding Chapter 13. 30-  Mandatory Organic Waste Disposal
  Regulations to Title 13 of the La Verne Municipal Code.

  Ordinance No. 1109 - AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF LA VERNE, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF LOS
  ANGELES, TO ADD CHAPTER 13. 30 - MANDATORY ORGANIC WASTE
  DISPOSAL REGULATIONS, TO TITLE 13 OF THE LA VERNE MUNICIPAL
  CODE.

11.  Council Comments  Council Member  Carder reported  on  the  year Christmas morning event.
  She thanked all the volunteers and staff who volunteered their time on
  Christmas morning to pass  out  the goodie bags.  In addition, she reported on

  the Gold Line Construction  time line.

  Council Member Crosby  wished  everyone  a  Happy New Year!  He encouraged

  residents to visit the City' s website on the Afflerbaugh and Paige Camp issue
  for talking points. He also  reported  on  the City' s Christmas  Morning event.  He
  stated  that the La Verne  library is open and  residents  should  visit.  He stated

  that City Manager Russi would meet with the County regarding a letter that
  was received regarding Base Line Road.

  Council Member Lau congratulated and welcomed new Police Chief Colleen

  about the Chamber of Commerce Newsletter and their articles. She urged

  be safe and kind.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis urged residents to send letters using the talking points
  posted on the City' s website on Afflerbaugh and Paige Camp to the Los
  Angeles Board of Supervisors and to attend the virtual meeting to be held on
  January 19, 2022 at 9: 30 a. m. He wished everyone a Happy New Year! He
  stated that the Christmas Morning event went well.  He thanked City staff, the
  residents who volunteered, the Community Emergency Response Team
  members (  CERT),  the La Verme Police RSVPS and the company who
  prewrapped the goody bags, for their participation in the Christmas Morning
  event. He reported on the Pomona Valley Transportation Committee ( PVTA)
  meeting and that the agency is looking for drivers. He spoke about celebrating
  Martin Luther King Day, civil rights and voting rights. He stated that January is
  National Human Trafficking Month and that February is Black History Month.

  Mayor Hepburn reported on the Christmas Morning event and stated that
  everyone  did an outstanding job. He thanked staff and especially his driver on
  the Christmas route. He wished everyone a Happy New Year! He stated that
  La Verne businesses were still struggling and urged residents to support them.
  He spoke about the Afflerbaugh and Paige talking points on the City' s website.
  He spoke  about  the Baseline issue.  He praised Los Angeles County Sherriff
  Villanueva for bringing in the FBI to investigate the recent murder of an off- duty
  Los Angeles Police Officer because District Attorney Gascon is not doing his
  job.
